latest_rss.title: Xi’s Purge and the War Over Taiwan
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia’s expulsion from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) was politically motivated; Chairman Xi Jinping’s purge of the PLA high command is best explained by his dissatisfaction with senior officers’ assessments of an operation against Taiwan and their willingness to act on Xi’s orders.



The Fujian-based generals Xi once trusted most, as well as the leadership of the Equipment Development Department and Rocket Force, and Zhang himself shared a professional caution about a cross-Strait war. Xi appears to have read their warnings as cowardice and resistance to the 2027 military readiness goal.



The purge shows political will emphasized over military professionalism. Military conflict is less likely in the short term while new officers enter their posts, but gray-zone pressure will likely escalate. A leadership consisting of compliant subordinates makes war increasingly likely over time.

latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Chinese intelligence efforts are increasingly moving away from human intelligence (HUMINT) collection to digital operations launched from within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Ministry of State Security (MSS), military intelligence, and others have started to employ online recruiting to replace face-to-face contact for foreign assets.



Beijing likely adopted the new model in response to the 2018 arrest of Xu Yanjun—the first MSS officer to be tried and convicted in the United States—which highlighted counterintelligence risks facing officers operating outside PRC borders.



The MSS is using LinkedIn en masse to recruit and develop assets overseas. These operations frequently involve headhunter-style approaches and commercial pretexts to collect resumes and gather intelligence.
